dicas.texto: Para transformar 20.000 em 100, estamos reduzindo o número. Qual operação matemática usamos para diminuir um valor mantendo a proporção?
Você precisa dividir o denominador atual (20.000) pelo denominador desejado (100). O resultado dessa divisão será o seu fator de escala.
Tente dividir 20.000 por 100. Quantas vezes o 100 cabe no 20.000? Esse é o número que você deve usar para dividir tanto o numerador quanto o denominador.
Se você cortar dois zeros de 20.000, o que sobra? Esse é o fator de escala que você deve usar na operação de divisão.
Lembre-se: uma porcentagem é uma razão onde o denominador é sempre 100. O numerador que você encontrar após a divisão já representa a sua porcentagem!
Divida o numerador original pelo mesmo fator de escala que você usou no denominador. O valor resultante é o número que vai sobre o 100.
Para a Parte 2, quanto é 100 dividido por 200? Pense em frações: 100/200 é o mesmo que 1/2.
Você tem 100 dividido por 200. Isso resulta em 0,5. Portanto, a porcentagem é 0,5%.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: A rate of defects compares the number of defective widgets with the total number of widgets.
Enter the weekly total as both numerator and denominator in the Total row, then use the defective count over 20,000 for each part.
Use 20,000 for every original denominator, 15 for the Part 1 numerator, and 100 for the Part 2 numerator.
Fill the six original-ratio cells with the whole amount in the Total row, then the two defective counts over the repeated total.
Equivalent ratios keep the same value when both terms are changed by the same multiplicative relationship.
Find the number that changes 20,000 into 100, then select division for both the numerator and denominator.
Since 20,000 divided by 200 equals 100, choose ÷ and enter 200 in both Part 1 scale-factor cells.
Use the operation that reduces 20,000 to 100, and use the same factor in both operation selectors and scale-factor fields.
An equivalent ratio changes both terms together, so the comparison between defects and total production stays unchanged.
Divide the Part 1 numerator by 200 and place the resulting value in the percentage numerator and percentage value fields.
Calculate 15 divided by 200, then enter that decimal in both Part 1 result fields.
Use the quotient of 15 and 200 for the two Part 1 result cells, while the denominator remains 100.
Both parts use the same weekly total, so both ratios need the same denominator transformation.
Compare the original denominator, 20,000, with the percentage denominator, 100, to determine the scale factor.
Because 20,000 divided by 200 equals 100, select ÷ for both Part 2 operation selectors and enter 200 twice.
Choose division, then use the factor that turns 20,000 into 100 in both Part 2 scale-factor fields.
The percentage ratio is equivalent to the original ratio because both terms are divided by the same factor.
Divide the Part 2 numerator, 100, by the scale factor 200 and enter the result in both Part 2 result fields.
Calculate 100 divided by 200, then use that decimal for the percentage numerator and percentage value.
Perform the final division of the Part 2 defective count by 200 and enter the resulting decimal in both cells.
A complete production total represents the entire group, so its percentage is the whole amount.
Use the Total row to represent the full production and verify that each part uses a denominator of 100 in the result.
The Total row should show 20,000 over 20,000 before scaling and 100 over 100 after scaling.
Finish the Total cells, confirm the two percentage rows, and click Done to submit the final value requested by the exercise.

exercicio.statement:
A factory makes 20,000 widgets every week.

Part 1) If 15 of the widgets one week are defective, what is the rate of defects?

Part 2) If the next week 100 of the widgets are defective, what percentage of the widgets are defective?

hints.message: A rate of defects compares the number of defective widgets with the total number of widgets.
Enter the weekly total as both numerator and denominator in the Total row, then use the defective count over 20,000 for each part.
Use 20,000 for every original denominator, 15 for the Part 1 numerator, and 100 for the Part 2 numerator.
Fill the six original-ratio cells with the whole amount in the Total row, then the two defective counts over the repeated total.

misconceptions.description: Aluno inverte a razão por não entender que 'defeitos por total' é o padrão.
misconceptions.feedback: The defective count belongs in the numerator and the total production belongs in the denominator. For Part 1, the ratio is 15 over 20,000, not 20,000 over 15.

nodes.description: Choose the operation and scale factor for the Part 1 ratio.
nodes.instruction: Choose the operation and scale factor for the Part 1 ratio.

hints.message: Equivalent ratios keep the same value when both terms are changed by the same multiplicative relationship.
Find the number that changes 20,000 into 100, then select division for both the numerator and denominator.
Since 20,000 divided by 200 equals 100, choose ÷ and enter 200 in both Part 1 scale-factor cells.
Use the operation that reduces 20,000 to 100, and use the same factor in both operation selectors and scale-factor fields.

nodes.description: Apply the Part 1 scale factor and complete its percentage result.
nodes.instruction: Apply the Part 1 scale factor and complete its percentage result.

hints.message: An equivalent ratio changes both terms together, so the comparison between defects and total production stays unchanged.
Divide the Part 1 numerator by 200 and place the resulting value in the percentage numerator and percentage value fields.
Calculate 15 divided by 200, then enter that decimal in both Part 1 result fields.
Use the quotient of 15 and 200 for the two Part 1 result cells, while the denominator remains 100.

misconceptions.description: Aluno divide o numerador pelo fator de escala em vez de dividir o denominador e aplicar a mesma operação no numerador.
misconceptions.feedback: The Part 1 numerator is 15, so dividing it by 200 does not produce 0.5. Apply the same division used to change 20,000 into 100: calculate 15 ÷ 200.

misconceptions.description: Aluno aplica o fator de escala como uma adição em vez de operação inversa à do denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You added the scale factor to the numerator. Because the denominator was divided by 200, the numerator must also be divided by 200.

nodes.description: Choose the operation and scale factor for the Part 2 ratio.
nodes.instruction: Choose the operation and scale factor for the Part 2 ratio.

hints.message: Both parts use the same weekly total, so both ratios need the same denominator transformation.
Compare the original denominator, 20,000, with the percentage denominator, 100, to determine the scale factor.
Because 20,000 divided by 200 equals 100, select ÷ for both Part 2 operation selectors and enter 200 twice.
Choose division, then use the factor that turns 20,000 into 100 in both Part 2 scale-factor fields.

nodes.description: Apply the Part 2 scale factor and complete its percentage result.
nodes.instruction: Apply the Part 2 scale factor and complete its percentage result.

hints.message: The percentage ratio is equivalent to the original ratio because both terms are divided by the same factor.
Divide the Part 2 numerator, 100, by the scale factor 200 and enter the result in both Part 2 result fields.
Calculate 100 divided by 200, then use that decimal for the percentage numerator and percentage value.
Perform the final division of the Part 2 defective count by 200 and enter the resulting decimal in both cells.

misconceptions.description: Aluno aplica o fator de escala como uma adição em vez de operação inversa à do denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You added the scale factor to the Part 2 numerator. Since the denominator was divided by 200, divide the numerator by 200 as well.

nodes.description: Complete the Total row, check both parts, and submit the final result.
nodes.instruction: Complete the Total row, check both parts, and submit the final result.

hints.message: A complete production total represents the entire group, so its percentage is the whole amount.
Use the Total row to represent the full production and verify that each part uses a denominator of 100 in the result.
The Total row should show 20,000 over 20,000 before scaling and 100 over 100 after scaling.
Finish the Total cells, confirm the two percentage rows, and click Done to submit the final value requested by the exercise.
